$comment: Handshake protocol 40 binds original parameter roots at exact opening-prefix reads. Protocol 39 adds affirmative unwritten parameter bindings for whole-slot identity, not concrete shape. Protocol 38 spells complete union premises and binds each constituent identity. Protocol 37 permits an exact anonymous local callable census only when its compiler symbol independently declares that node. Protocol 36 added localLiteralResult. Consumers still bind runtime identity and execution separately.
title: TypeFactsSchema v1 (latest semantic vocabulary)
description: Length-prefixed deterministic-CBOR request and response frames exchanged with solid-typefacts. Field names are the CBOR map keys. Optional fields are omitted, never null. Handshake protocol 55 (ADR 0095) makes a class a callee. A local-declaration demand whose location names a class is answered with the constructor whose body `new C(...)` runs, in both spellings -- `class C {...}` and the `const C = class {...}` every bundler emits for it, which are the same construction and must not certify differently. The transcript's resolved declaration is the class, because that is the identity the consumer demanded and bound its answer to; what the transcript censuses is the constructor, which is the code a construction runs. A construction evaluates the heritage clause's constructor, then every field initializer, then the constructor body, so everything in that sequence the constructor body does not contain refuses by name through `openReasons`: a heritage clause (three different claims live there -- the engine's base, this artifact's, or an expression's), a field initializer whether static or instance, a static block (which runs at class-definition time, not construction), a computed member name, a decorator on the class or any member, a parameter property (it assigns a field with no node of its own in the body), and an implicit constructor -- the last a deliberate over-refusal, since an implicit constructor with no heritage clause runs nothing at all but 'nothing runs' is a positive claim with no node to state it through. The refusals need no protocol number, because a consumer refuses on any nonempty `openReasons` whether or not it has seen the word; the number moves for the admitting side, since a protocol-54 producer answered `declarationNotExact` for every class and a consumer that reviewed only 54 would receive a constructor census under a demand it believed could answer only for a function. Handshake protocol 54 (ADR 0094) stops recording an uncensused invoking form for a **numeric-literal element access into an engine-owned indexed container**. A numeric index reaches an interface's index signature, and an index signature declares no property symbol, so such a read resolved nothing and was recorded as `property-access-unknown-accessor` exactly as a computed key is. Where the container is one the engine itself allocated -- a reviewed table holding `Array`, `ReadonlyArray`, `String`, `IArguments`, `RegExpExecArray`, `RegExpMatchArray`, `TemplateStringsArray` and the typed arrays -- the member reached is the engine's own storage and the read invokes nothing a user wrote. The premise has two halves and needs both: a default-library index signature cannot declare an accessor, and the object must be the engine's, which is why the **structural** interfaces `ArrayLike` and `ConcatArray` are absent even though the library declares their index too -- an ordinary object satisfies them while carrying whatever getter it likes, the same `Iterable` versus `Array` split earlier protocols draw. Every DOM indexed collection is absent as well: their indices are engine code in fact but were not reviewed. Three restrictions bound it -- element access only, an exact numeric literal only (a string-literal key names a declared member, and one that resolved to nothing is precisely the unresolved case), and read position only, because `subjectWrite` is load-bearing for the `writes` and `invalidates` domains and dropping the row would drop that mark. A union answers only when every constituent is in the table. This protocol **removes** rows a consumer previously received, and silence on this census is a positive claim, so a consumer that reviewed only protocol 53 would read the absence as a weaker statement than it is and the number moves. Handshake protocol 53 (ADR 0093) adds the `parameter-or-own-result` subject derivation and `subjectLocalLiteralResults`: a written parameter each of whose assigned values is either the caller's argument at this very slot or a value this program's own code allocated and returned, with one local-literal-result premise per source of the second kind. ADR 0091 rooted a written parameter only when every value was the caller's, which left `b = stringStyleToObject(b)` refusing; reading an own property of a value this program allocated reaches a data property (ADR 0044), so the binding holds one of two values and each is excused by a derivation already reviewed -- ADR 0090's structure. The arms are exhaustive because they are the binding's enumerated sources, and the spelling is deliberately apart from `parameter` because only one arm is the caller's: a consumer reading this one as that would say the caller installed whatever ran. A consumer binds every premise to a call row of the same transcript before reading any of them. Handshake protocol 52 (ADR 0092) adds `coercionSubjectParameters` beside a caller-rooted `coercionSubjectRoot`: the slots the form's operands rooted at, strictly increasing and deduplicated. Protocol 51 stated the agreed derivation as a diagnostic; this protocol makes it a premise, and a premise about the caller's value must say which slot -- the companion-fact invariant ADR 0047 states for `subjectParameter`. A coercion applies ToPrimitive to every operand, so the claim names every slot they rooted at rather than one receiver, and a consumer that reviewed only protocol 51 must not begin granting the derivation it read as a diagnostic. Handshake protocol 51 adds `coercionSubjectRoot` and `coercionSubjectRootRefusal` on a `coercion` form: the derivation **every** one of the form's ToPrimitive operands agreed on, or why they did not, with `mixed-operand-roots` for operands that each rooted but not at the same derivation. A coercing operator reaches Symbol.toPrimitive, valueOf and toString on every operand, so ADR 0042's argument -- the code that runs is the caller's exactly as a getter's is -- can only reach a coercion when every operand is the caller's; one operand this program built makes the form this program's act however the others rooted. Diagnostic and never a premise, like protocol 48's `subjectRootRefusal`, and deliberately separate from `subjectRoot`, which is an accessor's receiver and which a census admits. Handshake protocol 50 refines, and corrects the import leg: `imported-binding` is asked of the symbol **before** alias resolution, because the canonical symbol is the original declaration and a resolved import is otherwise indistinguishable from a local binding; a binding declared outside the artifact's own runtime source is `ambient-declaration`, which no premise in this family can reach because they all turn on what the artifact's own code assigned. It also refines `subjectRootRefusal`: a binding leg now names which of ADR 0044's conditions it failed — initialized from a call, uninitialized, initialized from a literal that is not data-only, or assigned somewhere — separately for module and function scope, and a parameter of a callable other than the censused one is `nested-parameter` rather than a local binding. Still a diagnostic and still never a premise; the coarse `module-binding` and `local-binding` remain for a shape none of the finer readings names. Handshake protocol 49 (ADR 0091) widens the `parameter` derivation to a parameter the body **writes**, when every value assigned to it is rooted at that same slot. ADR 0050 made this argument for a local binding; a parameter is the same question with one source that is the caller's by construction, the slot itself. The sources are the right-hand side of every plain assignment within the censused declaration, with a self-reference admitted co-inductively; a compound assignment, an update expression, a destructuring target and a `for…of`/`for…in` head refuse the whole binding rather than being skipped; two different slots refuse because the receipt names one; and a binding the write predicate calls written but for which no source was enumerated refuses, because the predicates disagreeing is the one way the join could be unsound. A consumer that reviewed only the unwritten reading must refuse this one, which is why the handshake moves although the spelling is unchanged. Handshake protocol 48 adds `subjectRootRefusal` on an uncensused invoking form: for an accessor form that roots no subject, which leg it fell off, over a closed vocabulary whose default `unclassified-subject` means no information. It is a **diagnostic and never a premise** — a consumer may print it, count it and choose what to review next by it, and may admit nothing on its account — and it is stated only where `subjectRoot` is empty, so a form carries a root or a reason and never both. Handshake protocol 47 (ADR 0090) adds the `parameter-default-literal` derivation: a parameter whose default is a **data-only literal** and which its body never writes is rooted at its own slot. Such a parameter holds exactly one of two values, the caller's argument or the object the default expression freshly created, and an accessor read is excused on each by a derivation already reviewed — `parameter` on the first and `own-literal` on the second — with the two arms exhaustive because a defaulted parameter is the argument when it is not `undefined` and the default otherwise. It is deliberately not spelled `parameter-default`, which names another rooted parameter and is caller-rooted on both arms; a consumer reading this one as that would say the caller installed whatever ran. The root does not propagate through a local binding, because what a property of the default's literal holds is an arbitrary expression of this program's, and only the accessor form kinds are stated. Handshake protocol 35 (ADR 0051) recognizes the explicit never type as a non-object fact before distributing union constituents. An empty constituent list without that explicit flag still refuses. The same predicate governs coercion forms, primitive operand premises, and primitiveCompletion: an explicit never completion states there is no normal object-valued result, not that a result type was unavailable. Caller argument premises and exact helper echoes still bind the type and its identity; a primitive completion never substitutes for censusing the callee's calls. Handshake protocol 34 (ADR 0050) widens the `parameter` derivation to a binding the file **writes**, when every value that binding can hold is rooted at one parameter. No flow analysis is involved and none is claimed: if every value the binding can hold is the caller's, then whichever one it holds at the read is the caller's, and which branch assigned it never comes up. The sources are the declaration's own initializer and the right-hand side of every plain assignment to it; a reference to the binding itself is admitted co-inductively, which is the chain rule applied to `a.b.c` written as a loop; and a declaration with no initializer contributes no source, because the value is then `undefined` and a member read of it throws before any lookup. A compound assignment, an update expression, a destructuring target and a `for…of`/`for…in` head each refuse the whole binding rather than being skipped, and sources rooted at two different slots refuse because the receipt names one. Handshake protocol 33 (ADR 0049) lets a `callArgumentPremise` cover the argument slots a call does **not** write as well as those it does: such a parameter receives `undefined` at run time, a primitive, which is a stronger premise than the `any` an unannotated parameter would otherwise carry. It is a semantic fact rather than a type one — the call has fewer arguments than the callee has parameters — so it is available where no declaration is, and it is what lets a premise chain survive a caller that omits an optional argument. A slot whose parameter has an **initializer** (the value is then the default), a **rest** parameter, a binding that is not a plain identifier, and a parameter the callee's own file **writes** are all skipped rather than stated; the list stays strictly increasing either way. Handshake protocol 32 (ADR 0048) adds the `parameter-result` derivation: the subject is the value a call to a **caller-supplied callee** handed back, and `subjectParameter` names the slot that callee was rooted at. What the caller's own function returned is the caller's, exactly as what its iterable yielded is (ADR 0042's `parameter-rooted-element`), so an accessor on it was installed by the caller and is analyzed in the caller's own artifact. Only a callee rooted as a plain `parameter` qualifies; the result of a call to a defaulted or derived one is a second hop this build does not review. Handshake protocol 31 (ADR 0047) lets an `instanceof` form carry `subjectRoot` too, for its **right** operand: the operator performs GetMethod(C, @@hasInstance) and calls it when there is one, so the whole question is whose `Symbol.hasInstance` the constructor could carry. Three answers are reviewed — `parameter`/`parameter-default`, a constructor the caller supplied, whatever it carries being the caller's; `default-library`, the engine's own constructor, whose method is `Function.prototype`'s and which carries no `subjectParameter` and no `subjectDeclaration`; and `own-class`, a class this program declares with **no heritage clause and no computed member name**, so nothing on its prototype chain can carry one, with `subjectDeclaration` naming the class. An imported constructor, a class with a superclass, a call result and a member read all state nothing. Handshake protocol 30 (ADR 0046) adds `spelling` on a `parameterPremise`: a form of the premise's type that resolves from a module which cannot name it directly, `import("<specifier>").<Name>`. A helper premise is written into a **JavaScript** module as a JSDoc `@param`, where a bare `Axis` resolves to nothing however precisely the package's declarations define it, so the premise was refused for a reason about spelling rather than about the code; the caller's twin, which does resolve the name, is where the spelling can be computed. It is a hint and never the premise — the printed `type` and the `identity` remain the whole falsifier, so a spelling that resolved to another type refuses the twin exactly as a wrong printed text does — and the established premise echoes it back byte for byte, which is why the handshake moves. A root premise carries neither identity nor spelling. Handshake protocol 29 (ADR 0045) adds `coercionPremise` on a `coercion` form and `primitiveCompletion` on every implementation transcript. A call to a module-local helper types as `any` in compiled JavaScript however well the package's declarations type the helper, so a sum of one refused wherever the premise had already typed everything else; the two fields are the missing half, in the callee's own words. `primitiveCompletion` says the checker's return type for the censused declaration — on the very program the census was classified over, the premise twin included — is a union of primitive types alone, which also settles the completion form, since a Promise and a Generator are not primitives. Because it belongs to the premise, the same helper censused under two argument premises may state it under one and not the other, and a consumer may read it only from the transcript it demanded under the premise it recorded. Handshake protocol 28 (ADR 0044) adds a third `subjectRoot` value, `own-literal`, which is not a claim about the caller: the subject is a binding this program initialized from an **object or array literal**, or from an object pattern's **rest element**, whose every own property the specification creates with CreateDataPropertyOrThrow. Reading any member of such a value — a computed key included, which is the case the checker resolves no symbol for and refuses — reaches a data property or the engine's own prototype chain. It carries `subjectDeclaration`, the exact range of the binding, and **no** `subjectParameter`; a consumer must place that declaration in the analyzed artifact's own runtime source before reading the premise. The literal must install no `get`/`set` member and no `__proto__` member, the binding must have exactly one declaration, and nothing in its file may write it. An array pattern's rest element is excluded: its elements come from the source's iterator, which is an iteration question. Handshake protocol 27 (ADR 0043) accompanies every stated `subjectParameter` with `subjectRoot`, the derivation that rooted the subject at that slot, over a closed two-value set. `parameter` is ADR 0034's premise unchanged and now covers three further spellings of the same value: the parameter itself or a read chain through it, a name an **object binding pattern in parameter position** binds when the parameter carries no default, and a name a **local variable declaration** binds from an initializer that is itself rooted, taken to a fixpoint — naming an intermediate does not change whose value it is. `parameter-default` is the new claim: the slot carries a **default** that is a reference to a parameter rooted the first way, so the value is the caller's argument at this slot or the caller's argument at the default's, caller-supplied under either branch. A rest parameter, a rest element, a binding element or parameter pattern carrying its own default, a name bound by a `for…of`/`for…in` head, and a symbol with more than one declaration are all excluded. A consumer must refuse a spelling it has not reviewed rather than read it as the weaker one, which is why the handshake moves although the field is additive. Handshake protocol 26 (ADR 0042) covers the iteration protocol. An `iteration-protocol` form may carry `subjectParameter`, the parameter its iterated value is rooted at, on a `forOfStatement`, a `spreadElement` or an array binding pattern; `implementationCall` may carry `calleeIteratedParameter`, the parameter-rooted iterable whose iteration produced the callee, stated only for a plain non-`await` `for…of` head declaring one unwritten binding; and a **rest parameter's** array is no longer recorded as an iteration form at all, because the engine constructs it, so iterating or spreading it reaches `Array.prototype` and nothing else — a syntactic fact its `any[]` type cannot supply. Handshake protocol 25 (ADR 0041) lets two further form shapes carry `subjectParameter`: an object or JSX prop **spread**, whose operand the runtime reads every own enumerable property of, and a **binding element** of an object pattern, whose subject is the value the outermost enclosing pattern destructures (a rest element included). Both are reads, so `subjectWrite` is absent for them. A protocol-24 producer roots only a property or element access, so a consumer reading a subject on these node kinds must require this protocol. Handshake protocol 24 (ADR 0040) states an uncensused accessor form's `subjectParameter` in **write** position as well as read, and adds `subjectWrite` beside it saying which position the access is in: an assignment target, a compound assignment or an update expression sets it, and a compound or update form runs the getter before the setter. A protocol-23 consumer only ever received a subject for a read, so reading the subject without the position would read a write into the caller's object as a read of it, and the handshake moves although the field is additive. `set-accessor` joins `get-accessor` and `property-access-unknown-accessor` as a kind that may carry a subject; `delete` still carries none. Handshake protocol 23 (ADR 0038, helper premises) adds optional `parameterPremises` on `exportValueDemand` — stated only beside `localDeclarationLocation`, the types the consumer asks the local declaration's form census be classified under — optional `callArgumentPremises` on `exportImplementationTranscript` — for each call of a *premised* census whose callee is a declaration in the program's own runtime source, the type each informative written argument slot carried on the twin, which is what a consumer hands back as the callee's premise — and optional `identity` on `parameterPremise`, the producer's opaque binding of a premise text to a declaration, echoed byte for byte. A local declaration's transcript may now state `parameterPremises`, equal to the demand's, when its census was classified under them; a protocol-22 consumer refused any premise on a local declaration and never asked for one, so the handshake moves. Handshake protocol 22 (ADR 0038) adds optional `parameterPremises` and `parameterPremiseRefusal` on `exportImplementationTranscript`: when present, the uncensused-form census of that implementation was classified with each parameter bound to the type the export's declared call signature gives its position — the signature a consumer compiles against and a synthesized veto samples from — rather than to the implicit `any` of an unannotated JavaScript parameter, so a coercion or iteration over a parameter declared `number` records no form. An absent list is the strictly more refusing classification over the parameters' own types and never a premise; a present one is a condition a consumer records on whatever it closes. The handshake moves because an empty form list gains a new meaning on a premised transcript. Handshake protocol 18 (ADR 0034) adds optional `subjectParameter` on `uncensusedInvokingForm` — the parameter of the transcript's own declaration at which a read accessor's receiver chain is rooted, stated only for a plain, uninitialized, non-rest parameter written nowhere in its file in a declaration mentioning neither `arguments` nor `eval` — and optional `callReceiver`/`thisParameter` on `implementationCall` for a `.call`/`.apply` whose resolved callee is the default library's Function.prototype member. An absent fact on an older producer is never a statement that the subject is unrooted, so the handshake moves. Handshake protocol 16 adds optional `returnSite.parameter`: positive identity of an unchanged whole input binding, never inferred from a missing fact or concrete return type. Protocol 15 splits control-flow incompleteness into classes and stops withholding call rows. `controlFlowCensus.incompleteness` states, per construct and at its exact location, which of two different things a `unsupported` marker means: `reachability-lower-bound`, a construct walked in full whose enclosed sites are all recorded and none called `unreachable` on its account, so only the *guarantee* is missing and a may-execute enumeration stands; or `flow-unaccounted`, a construct whose flow the census cannot account for at all, which is also the classifier's default so an unclassified marker refuses on arrival. In the same protocol the implementation call census no longer drops a call that lies in a region a `break` or `continue` makes non-universal: the row is emitted with `reach` `unknown`, the weakest non-negative value, because a dropped row is silence and silence is indistinguishable from the absence of the call. An *absent* `incompleteness` beside a nonempty `unsupported` is a producer with no classification, which a consumer must refuse, and no decoder can separate it from a present empty one — so the handshake protocol is the discriminator here too. Handshake protocol 14 added the two facts an implementation census needs: `uncensusedInvokingForms` on `exportImplementationTranscript`, one row per syntactic position that can invoke user code and that `calls` — which holds `CallExpression` and `NewExpression` only — does not record, over a closed twelve-kind vocabulary whose default is the refusing `unclassified-invoking-form`; and `localDeclarationLocation` on `exportValueDemand`, answered by `localDeclaration`, an implementation transcript for the function-like declaration at an exact source range, which is the only way to reach a declaration no export names. An *absent* `uncensusedInvokingForms` is a producer with no opinion and a present empty one is the positive claim that every walked form was a call, a construction, or provably non-invoking; no decoder can separate them, so the handshake protocol is the discriminator and the number moves rather than the fields being merely additive. Protocol 13 added `calleeSources` to the implementation call census: the traced value provenance of the callee expression, from the same tracer and under the same gates that answer `argumentSources` for an argument and `sources` for a return site, with an empty list meaning the producer traced nothing and never a negative claim about the callee. It coexists with `target`/`targetName`/`targetModule`/`declaration`/`calleeParameter`, which state the callee's *resolution* and are unchanged. Protocol 12 added `argumentSources`: per written argument slot, the traced value provenance of the expression written there, and narrowed that tracer's identifier arm to a single-declaration array binding element that is never assigned and carries neither a rest token nor a default, so a `ReturnSite.sources` a protocol-11 producer states may be withheld here. Protocol 11 split the callable-path census into declared members and apparent leaves: every path fact carries `apparent`, true for a member a value has only through the compiler's global-Function augmentation on a node with call or construct signatures. V1 is the sole active lifecycle schema. The retained table remains Wire schema v18 because invocation and exported-value transcripts are demand-shaped side answers rather than retained rows. The producer hashes this file and reports the digest in its startup handshake; both executables additionally ship in build-ID lockstep.

bytes.description: CBOR byte string; JSON Schema has no byte-string type.

moduleInventoryDemand.description: Selects how much of the resolved module graph one modules operation answers. The module inventory itself is unconditional. Imports with no importPaths covers every file the program included.

projectReferenceMapping.description: The compiler's own pairing of one input file with the declaration file emitted from it. Present only where a configured project reference covers the file, and the only declaration-to-implementation pairing TypeScript maintains. A shipped .d.ts beside a .js never has one.

moduleFact.description: One file the TypeScript program resolved and included, as the program holds it. For a module reached through a symlink the path is the realpath.

packageIdentity.description: The nearest enclosing package.json found by the compiler's own package-scope lookup, and that manifest's own name and version. An absent name or version is a fact about the manifest, not a lookup failure.

resolverPackageId.description: The package identity the resolver itself recorded while resolving one specifier. It can name a different package than the nearest enclosing manifest. subpath is the selected file's path within the package, not the exports key that led there.

moduleImportFact.description: One module specifier occurrence and what the compiler's resolver recorded for it. resolvedPath is empty exactly when resolution is unresolved. symlinkPath is populated only where the resolver's own realpath differed from the path it walked. includedPath is populated only where the program parses a different file than the one resolved, which happens for a configured project reference's declaration output and for nothing else.

compactDemands.description: Demand snapshot with one string dictionary per frame; index 0 is the empty string. Each group is [pathIndex, packedRows] where packedRows holds unsigned LEB128 (flags << 1 | hasQuery, startDelta, length) triples, each optionally followed by (queryPath, queryStart, queryLength). Bit 9 requests runtimeValueDomain, bit 10 requests callResultDomain, bit 11 requests constantValue, bit 12 requests arrayShape, bit 13 requests tupleShape, bit 14 requests libraryTypes, bit 15 requests primitiveValueDomain, bit 16 requests constructability, bit 17 requests primitiveLiteralCandidates, and bit 18 requests parameterObjectShape.

controlFlowIncompleteness.description: One construct whose flow this control-flow census does not fully model, at its exact location, classified by what is missing. `reachability-lower-bound` is a construct walked in full — every enclosed site is recorded and none is called `unreachable` on its account — whose *guarantee* alone is unmodelled, so a may-execute enumeration of the callables inside it stands. `flow-unaccounted` is a construct whose flow the census cannot account for in either direction, and it is also the classifier's default, so a marker nobody classified refuses on arrival. The class enum is closed: an unrecognized string rejects the whole transcript. Every marker in `unsupported` has at least one row here and every row's marker is in `unsupported`.

uncensusedInvokingForm.description: One syntactic position that can invoke user code and that the implementation call census does not record. The kind enum is closed: an unrecognized string rejects the whole transcript rather than degrading to an unknown row. An absent uncensusedInvokingForms array is a producer with no opinion, which a consumer must refuse; a present empty array is the positive claim that every walked form was a call, a construction, or provably non-invoking.

localLiteralResultPremise.description: Every normal completion of this exact synchronous local callee returns the same unwritten local data-only literal allocation. A terminal return covers fallthrough, and all return sites are enumerated. The consumer must bind and census the named call; an absent fact proves nothing.

initialParameterRead.description: Protocol 45: caller origin at one exact property use. An unmarked row binds an opening read; positional binds a use before every possible store; firstIterationOnly limits origin to the first loop entry. undefinedDefault binds the sole store, a body-level strict void-0 guard assigning a local empty array, and limits origin to defined caller arguments. Its use must be the first reference other than the exact guard operand and store target, and must follow the guard; at most one such row may name a parameter. These three limitations are mutually exclusive. Limited origin never proves guaranteed execution or the identity of a later use.

originalHelperRead.description: Protocol 46: one-hop possible synchronous read of an original caller input through an exact stable local helper. No guarantee, member shape, or later identity is implied.

invocation.description: The form the selected signature is invoked through (ADR 0105, handshake protocol 59). Stated as "construct" for a class export and absent for a call, because absence is what every producer below this protocol meant by saying nothing. A consumer must read it: the census of a construction is a census of a constructor body, and reading it as a call would describe an invocation the class cannot accept.

parameterPremise.description: One parameter of the transcript's implementation bound to a type, under which uncensusedInvokingForms was classified (ADR 0038, handshake protocols 22 and 23). On an export's root implementation, type is the declared type's printed form, byte-identical to the export transcript's selectedSignature.parameters[index].value.type.text, and identity is absent. On a local declaration's transcript the entries equal the demand's exportValueDemand.parameterPremises, which the consumer copied from the caller's callArgumentPremises for the call it followed; identity is the producer's opaque binding of the text to a declaration (type flags and declaration positions), compared byte for byte and never interpreted by a consumer.

coercionPremise.description: What one `coercion` form's clearance would rest on (ADR 0045, handshake protocol 29): every operand the coercion applies ToPrimitive to is either provably a primitive by its own type — those are not listed, because a primitive has no `Symbol.toPrimitive`, `valueOf` or `toString` to reach — or the result of one of these calls into the program's own runtime source. Absent when some operand is neither, which is every shape no ADR has reviewed. Stating it is never a claim that the form clears: a consumer grants it only by matching each call to a row of the same transcript's `calls`, taking that row's own callee and premise, and requiring the callee's transcript to state `primitiveCompletion`. Four value-carrying shapes are followed to reach an operand: a conditional and the short-circuit operators (every arm must qualify), and a reference to a local binding the file declares once, writes nowhere and initializes.

notCallableValue.description: The demanded export's runtime value cannot be invoked (ADR 0099, handshake protocol 56): every constituent of its type has no call signature, no construct signature, is not callable without signatures, and is not any, unknown, never, an error, or an instantiable type. Stated only on a transcript that is otherwise open with the single reason valueNotCallable and carries declaration. kind is primitive when every constituent is a primitive type and object otherwise; type is the checker's spelling of the whole type.

importedModuleMember.description: The module specifier exactly as an import statement wrote it, and the exported name the imported binding refers to (ADR 0104, handshake protocol 58). Stated beside subjectRoot "dependency-member" and never beside a refusal. The specifier is not a package identity: a consumer decides for itself whether it names a dependency it has reviewed, and the producer refuses a relative or absolute specifier, a namespace import, a default import, and a locally assigned binding.

defaultLibraryAlias.description: The demanded export is a default-library member by identity (ADR 0103, handshake protocol 57): a const binding, never written in the file, whose initializer is a property access whose object and member both resolve to default-library symbols, with the member declared on the named container's interface and neither container nor member written, deleted, or escaping as anything but a read or a call. Stated beside the transcript's existing open reason rather than instead of it, because whether the named member is safe to close a call domain on is the consumer's reviewed decision: Object.keys invokes no caller callable, Array.prototype.map does, and the two are stated identically here. A consumer with no reviewed entry for the member must read this as not stated.

callArgumentPremise.description: The type each informative written argument slot of one call carried on the twin a premised uncensused-form census ran over (handshake protocol 23). call is the location of a row of the transcript's calls, in the original file's bytes; arguments has strictly increasing indexes, and a slot it omits was `any` or unspellable. Stated only on a transcript that also states parameterPremises, and only for a call with no spread whose callee is an identifier resolving to a declaration in the program's own runtime source.

lifecycleResponse.description: Analyze carries at most one opaque tableTransition. The transition proves its base project, generation, and state token and selects full or delta mode internally. An absent transition reuses the retained table. The modules operation instead carries modules, moduleImports, and unknownImportPaths as plain rows: the resolved module graph is a property of the accepted program rather than of a demand set, so it takes no part in retained table identity.

tableTransition.description: Opaque full-or-delta Wire table transition. The active lifecycle schema emits Wire table schema v17. V15 introduced untypedCallable (tag 4), v16 added primitive literal candidates, and v17 added parameter object-construction shapes; older table schemas remain frozen and reject facts they cannot represent.

sourceArena.description: Filesystem path to a temporary file holding every source body back to back, sliced by sourceLengths. Implies a producer and client that share a filesystem.

modules.description: Every file the program included, ordered by path. A modules operation always answers it.

moduleImports.description: Resolved provenance for the requested files' module specifiers, ordered by importing path then by specifier start byte.

unknownImportPaths.description: Requested import paths the program does not hold, ordered by path. Reported rather than dropped so a caller can tell a file with no imports from a file that was never analyzed.
